docs.title: swarmboard
docs.text:
One board. The whole swarm.

A CLI-first kanban board (swrm) that any number of agents can work on at the same time — with a live terminal view and an immediate change feed. No server, no dependencies.

Most kanban tools assume one human at a keyboard. swarmboard assumes a swarm: many agents (and humans) claiming, commenting, blocking, and completing cards concurrently — and everyone sees it happen immediately.

  • Concurrency-safe by design — one SQLite database in WAL mode; claims are atomic, so two agents can never grab the same card.
  • Immediate change feed — every mutation lands in an append-only event log in the same transaction. swrm watch streams it; swrm dash renders it.
  • Terminal-first — the board is the terminal. Open swrm dash and watch the swarm move.
  • Zero dependencies — a single Python 3 file (swrm) using only the standard library.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: Command What it does swrm init create the board database swrm add "title" [--body B] [--assignee A] [--priority N] [--label L]... [--parent ID]... create a card; starts ready, or todo if any parent isn't done swrm ls [--status S] [--assignee A] [--label L] list cards swrm board static column view swrm dash (aliases dashboard, live) live-updating board view — --once, --follow, --interval, --feed N swrm show <id> card detail + parents/children + full event history swrm claim <id> / swrm claim --any [--assignee A] [--ttl SECONDS] atomically claim a ready card swrm release <id> [--force] release a claim back to ready swrm reclaim [id] [--force] release expired claims back to ready swrm complete <id> --summary "..." mark done; auto-promotes children whose parents are all done swrm block <id> --reason "..." / swrm unblock <id> park / revive a card swrm move <id> <status> set status directly (todo ready doing done blocked archived) swrm assign <id> <agent> reassign swrm edit <id> [--title T] [--body B] [--priority N] [--label L]... edit fields swrm link <parent> <child> / swrm unlink <parent> <child> dependency links; linking demotes a runnable child to todo until parents finish swrm comment <id> "text" add a note to the card's history swrm rm <id> / swrm rm <status> / swrm rm --all archive one card, all cards in a status (rm done, rm blocked), or the whole board swrm prune [--dry-run] permanently delete archived cards, their links and their events swrm events [--task ID] [--limit N] dump the change feed swrm watch [--json] [--since N] [--interval S] stream the change feed live (Ctrl-C to stop) swrm serve [--host H] [--port P] [--passkey K] run the leader server (default 127.0.0.1:8765) so other PCs can connect via KANBAN_URL; --passkey requires followers to authenticate

docs.title: Global flags
docs.text:
All commands accept:

Flag Env var Meaning --db PATH $KANBAN_DB board database location --actor NAME $KANBAN_ACTOR who is acting --url URL $KANBAN_URL run against a remote leader over HTTP --passkey SECRET $KANBAN_PASSKEY authenticate to the leader --json — machine-readable output

docs.title: The CLI
docs.text: Single file: swrm (Python 3 stdlib only). Schema: tasks, links (parent→child), events (append-only audit feed).

docs.title: These docs
docs.text:
This site is built with MkDocs + the Material theme. Sources are the Markdown files in docs/; config is mkdocs.yml at the repo root.

pip install -r docs/requirements.txt
python3 -m mkdocs serve        # live preview at http://127.0.0.1:8000
python3 -m mkdocs build        # writes static HTML to docs/site/

The built site in docs/site/ is plain static HTML — serve it with anything:

python3 -m http.server -d docs/site 8000     # or nginx / GitHub Pages / etc.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/Nergy101/swarmboard.git
cd swarmboard
chmod +x swrm                   # already executable
ln -s "$PWD/swrm" ~/.local/bin/swrm   # optional: put it on PATH
swrm init                       # create ./.kanban/kanban.db

Requires Python 3.8+. Nothing else — swrm is a single file using only the standard library.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Everything is configurable via flags or environment variables:

Setting Flag Env var Default Board location --db PATH $KANBAN_DB ./.kanban/kanban.db Actor name --actor NAME $KANBAN_ACTOR $USER Remote leader --url URL $KANBAN_URL (local mode) Leader passkey --passkey SECRET $KANBAN_PASSKEY (none)

Every command also accepts --json for machine-readable output.

Remote mode

Set $KANBAN_URL (or pass --url) and every command runs against the leader over HTTP instead of a local database — see Leader-follower mode.

docs.title: Across multiple PCs — leader-follower mode
docs.text:
SQLite is single-host (WAL locking doesn't survive network filesystems), so the board file lives on one leader PC; every other PC is a thin follower that talks HTTP. All commands work unchanged — set one env var on the followers:

# PC1 — the leader (owns the database)
swrm serve --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8765 --passkey s3cret   # bind 127.0.0.1 for localhost-only

# PC2, PC3, ... — followers
export KANBAN_URL=http://pc1:8765 KANBAN_PASSKEY=s3cret  # or --passkey s3cret per command
swrm add "task from pc2" --assignee qa
swrm claim --any --assignee qa --actor qa
swrm dash                                     # live board, long-polled from the leader
swrm watch --json                             # NDJSON feed, long-polled from the leader

PC2 (follower)              PC1 (leader)
swrm claim --any ──HTTP──>  swrm serve ──> SQLite (WAL, atomic claims)
swrm dash       <──GET /snapshot / /events?since=N (long-poll)──
  • The leader runs the exact same command functions in-process, so claims stay atomic across all PCs — two followers can never grab the same card.
  • watch/dash on followers long-poll GET /events?since=N / GET /snapshot, so the live feed works over the network with ~LAN-latency updates.
  • --url http://pc1:8765 works per-command as an alternative to $KANBAN_URL.

docs.title: Passkey authentication
docs.text: swrm serve --passkey SECRET (or $KANBAN_PASSKEY) makes the leader require an X-Swrm-Passkey: SECRET header on every request — anything missing/wrong gets 401. Followers set the same secret via KANBAN_PASSKEY or --passkey. Without a passkey the API is open — trusted LANs/VPNs only, or front it with an auth-ing reverse proxy.

docs.title: HTTP endpoints
docs.text: Endpoint Description POST /cmd/<command> any CLI command, JSON args GET /events?since=N&timeout=25 long-poll change feed GET /events?max=1 latest event GET /snapshot?feed=N full board snapshot GET /health health check

docs.title: Multi-agent usage (one PC)
docs.text:
Point every agent at the same board and give each a distinct actor name:

export KANBAN_DB=/shared/project/.kanban/kanban.db

# orchestrator fans work out — children wait for their parents automatically
T1=$(swrm add "research costs" --assignee researcher --json | jq -r .id)
T2=$(swrm add "research perf"  --assignee researcher --json | jq -r .id)
swrm add "synthesize" --assignee analyst --parent "$T1" --parent "$T2"

# workers self-serve from the board
swrm claim --any --assignee researcher --actor researcher   # atomic claim
swrm comment "$T1" "started" --actor researcher
swrm complete "$T1" --actor researcher --summary "costs done"

# anyone can watch the swarm live
swrm dash

Parallel add/claim/complete calls from many processes never lose events. Claims are atomic: two agents can never grab the same card.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
swrm init                                   # create the board
swrm add "research costs" --assignee researcher
swrm add "ship it" --parent t_aa11          # starts in todo until parent is done
swrm claim --any --assignee researcher --actor researcher
swrm comment t_aa11 "started" --actor researcher
swrm complete t_aa11 --actor researcher --summary "costs done"
swrm dash                                   # live board

docs.title: Watch it live
docs.text:
swrm dash          # full-screen live board, re-rendered every 0.5s (alias: swrm dashboard)

 KANBAN /proj/.kanban/kanban.db   2026-11-17T23:21:40Z
todo:1  ready:2  doing:1  blocked:0  done:12
----------------------------------------------------------------
TODO (1)        READY (2)       DOING (1)       BLOCKED (0)  DONE (12)
--------------  --------------  --------------  -----------  ------
┌────────────┐  ┌────────────┐  ┌────────────┐
│research    │  │ship the    │  │polish      │
│costs       │  │API         │  │dashboard   │
│t_aa11 P1   │  │t_bb22 P3   │  │t_9f4b P0   │
│@dev        │  │@qa         │  │[dev 14m59s]│
└────────────┘  └────────────┘  └────────────┘
 feed: #41 dev claimed t_9f4b ...  #42 qa done t_cc33 ...

Each card is a bordered box (tinted with its column color): title first, with a dim meta line underneath (id, priority, assignee or claim time left).

doing rows show which worker picked up which task and the time left on their claim. In the live full-screen view the column headers and feed stay pinned; move the cursor with ↑/↓/←/→ (or hjkl) and press Enter or click a card to open a detail modal (history, parents/children, body) — click another card to switch the modal to it, click outside to close; q closes the modal / quits. swrm dash --once prints one snapshot (default when piped); swrm watch --json is the NDJSON feed for piping into other agents.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
todo ──(all parents done)──> ready ──(claim)──> doing ──> done
                                            └───────> blocked ──(unblock)──> ready

Claims expire (default TTL 900 s, --ttl to change); swrm reclaim releases stale ones back to ready.

docs.title: The swarmboard skill
docs.text:
.vibe/skills/swarmboard/SKILL.md is the orchestrator playbook for routing a swarm through this board (load it as /swarmboard; adapted from the kanban-orchestrator workflow).

It covers:

  • Decomposition patterns — how to break a goal into cards and wire dependencies with swrm link / --parent.
  • Parent-gating — children stay in todo until all parents are done; swrm complete auto-promotes them.
  • Anti-temptation rules — "route, don't execute": the orchestrator adds and links cards, workers swrm claim --any and do the work.
  • Stuck-card recovery — swrm reclaim for expired claims, swrm block / swrm unblock for parked work, swrm events to audit what happened.

All expressed in swrm commands, so any agent with the skill loaded can drive the board the same way.
